title: Payroll credential harvesting campaign
text: Between 2 and 3 February, employees of several logistics firms received emails claiming that their salary slip was available. The message urged recipients to confirm their identity before the payment date. The link pointed to hxxps://payroll-portal-secure[.]example/verify, a cloned single sign-on page hosted on 198.51.100.24. Submitted usernames and passwords were posted to a PHP collector. The sender domain payroll-portal-secure.example was registered two days before the campaign. No attachment was used; the operation relied entirely on credential theft through a spoofed portal.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Second wave of the payroll portal phishing
text: The payroll-themed operation observed earlier this month resumed with new wording about a bonus payment. The kit is unchanged and still posts stolen credentials to 198.51.100.24. A new lookalike domain, payroll-bonus-secure.example, was added alongside the original payroll-portal-secure.example. Emails were sent through a compromised newsletter account, which explains the valid SPF results. Recipients were mainly HR and accounting staff of mid-sized companies.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Payroll portal phishing - infrastructure update
text: Tracking of the payroll credential harvesting operation shows a migration of the collector to a new server while 198.51.100.24 remains in use as a redirector. The phishing page is now reachable at https://payroll-portal-secure.example/login. Analysts noticed the kit added a CAPTCHA to evade automated scanners. Indicators from the previous reports remain relevant and should stay on block lists.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Tax refund phishing with PDF lure
text: During the tax season, citizens received emails announcing a refund. The PDF attachment, MD5 5b1eb6f3231cabb696e9ee18564b11d6, contained a button to http://tax-refund-claim.test/form where victims entered their bank account and identity information. The sender display name copied the tax administration. The campaign targeted personal addresses rather than corporate inboxes and was relayed by a botnet of compromised servers.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Glacier ransomware targeting virtualisation hosts
text: Glacier, a Linux variant of a ransomware family, targets hypervisors. Attackers log in through exposed remote access services with stolen credentials, shut down virtual machines and encrypt the disk images. The encryptor (SHA-256 ba7b589ca11313cedb46bde7a25a8dab62d626307867b7cdc7d8b79423c04c36) is downloaded from hxxp://203.0.113[.]99/g.sh. Entire clusters become unavailable in minutes, which multiplies the impact compared with workstation encryption. Victims should restrict management interfaces to dedicated networks.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Glacier ransomware new Linux build
text: A new build of the Glacier Linux locker adds intermittent encryption: only parts of each large file are encrypted to speed up the attack. The binary (SHA-256 0a9e39787748450bce57034693698405e02dd8b83708d3ed22e9dff737e2d43b) is still retrieved from 203.0.113.99. The ransom note now includes a chat identifier and a deadline of 72 hours. Hypervisor administrators should disable unnecessary shell access.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Ransomware using safe mode reboot
text: A ransomware strain called Hollowkey reboots Windows machines into safe mode to prevent security tools from starting, then encrypts files. It modifies registry keys to ensure execution in safe mode and deletes recovery points. The sample MD5 is 9a2abda370892bfa4398a22a8d3b0ca0 and its configuration contains the contact address on hollowkey-recovery.test. Encrypted files end with .hkey.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Glacier operators exploit weak hypervisor passwords
text: Glacier operators continue to target virtualisation clusters, this time using weak passwords on management interfaces exposed to the internet. After logging in, they encrypt virtual disks with the locker downloaded from http://203.0.113.99/g.sh. Victims include two hosting providers, which affected hundreds of downstream customers.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: StealRay information stealer analysis
text: StealRay is a commodity information stealer sold as a subscription. Once executed it collects saved browser passwords, cookies, cryptocurrency wallet files and screenshots, compresses them and uploads the archive over HTTPS to cdn-telemetry-sync.example. The analysed sample has SHA-256 97d5bba19c2dc2af1f218286daaacb3e3a5e6d8a98b1fb97724c0fd54c8f0e4f. The C2 server 203.0.113.88 also serves configuration updates. The malware deletes itself after exfiltration, leaving few traces on disk.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: StealRay distributed through cracked software
text: New StealRay samples are distributed through websites offering cracked games and software. Users who run the fake installer get their browser credentials stolen within seconds. Stolen logs are sent to cdn-telemetry-sync.example and to a backup server 203.0.113.89. The installer has MD5 474a5c7bdc9df9d12d19908765b83bdd. Stolen credentials are later sold on underground markets.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Trojanised software package in a public repository
text: A package published in a public code repository imitated a popular logging library. Its install script downloaded a backdoor from hxxp://pkg-mirror-cdn[.]example/lib/init.bin and executed it on developer machines. The backdoor (SHA-256 4f86a8637c572d164e575243aa1735095c5da68e91bf5d8ad859499914dec34b) stole SSH keys and cloud tokens. The package was downloaded 1,200 times before removal.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: StealRay panel exposed
text: Researchers found an exposed StealRay administration panel on 203.0.113.88. It contained logs from 4,000 victims including browser passwords and session cookies. The panel software matches the stealer sample 97d5bba19c2dc2af1f218286daaacb3e3a5e6d8a98b1fb97724c0fd54c8f0e4f. Affected companies were notified through national CERTs.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Mass scanning for vulnerable file transfer servers
text: Following the disclosure of a path traversal flaw in a managed file transfer product (CVE-2099-0602), honeypots recorded large-scale scanning from 203.0.113.190, 203.0.113.191 and 198.51.100.55. Successful exploitation allows reading arbitrary files, including configuration files containing credentials. Exposed instances should be patched or placed behind a VPN.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Firewall management interface command injection
text: A command injection in the web management interface of a firewall series (CVE-2099-0815) allows remote attackers to execute operating system commands as root. Exploitation attempts were observed from 192.0.2.99 targeting management interfaces exposed to the internet. The vendor recommends restricting the management interface to trusted networks and upgrading the firmware.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Data theft through managed file transfer vulnerability
text: An extortion group exploited the managed file transfer path traversal (CVE-2099-0602) to steal files from dozens of organisations without deploying any encryption. The exploitation came from 198.51.100.55 and a downloader script was retrieved from http://mft-sync-update.example/a.py. Victims were contacted by email with samples of their stolen data.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Firewall command injection exploited by state-linked actor
text: The firewall command injection (CVE-2099-0815) is now exploited by a state-linked actor dubbed Basalt Crane. After exploitation, the actor installs a passive implant that listens for specially crafted packets. The exploitation infrastructure includes 192.0.2.99 and fw-telemetry-update.example.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).
